title: High-touch intake heuristics and SLA simulator
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an operationally-safe, repeatable intake pipeline for top-account and escalated requests that combines an automated heuristic scorer with a lightweight SLA impact simulator. The goal is to reduce time-to-decision for VIP asks, ensure predictable commitments to customers, and quantify risk to existing roadmap SLAs before committing scope. This will power a fast-track lane in the roadmap intake flow as well as an internal simulation view for PMs and Sales leaders.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Heuristic scorer returns a ranked list for sample dataset of 150 historical VIP requests matching historical prioritization at >= 78% precision at top-5. 2) SLA simulator shows projected latency/cost/regional-capacity impacts for next 90 days for accepted vs deferred scenarios. 3) UI in Console exposes score + simulator outputs and a 'propose-commitment' button that creates a templated engagement note. 4) Playbook updated with rollback and fallback rules and approved by legal and security reviewers. 5) Integration tests added that validate no commits are allowed without capacity-availability signal from Dedicated service.
notes:
- Use composite scoring: ARR-weighted account score, strategic alignment tag, churn-risk signal from CRM, regulatory friction, estimated engineering effort (T-shirt), and existing commitments.
- Simulator will use historical throughput & latency traces from the Console telemetry pipeline (BigQuery) plus Dedicated capacity forecasts.
- Initial rollout limited to EMEA + NA high-touch accounts. APAC to follow after capacity baseline.
- Playbook must define 'fast-track' vs 'scoped-pilot' and stakeholder ack requirements.
decisions: 1) Scoring model: start with linear weighted sum (weights tunable via Console) and surface counterfactuals rather than fully automated accept. 2) Human-in-the-loop required for any commitment > $200k ARR or > 3 sprint-equivalent engineering effort. 3) SLA simulator will not alter Dedicated autoscaling policies automatically — only advisory outputs for PM/SE to approve changes. 4) PRD stored in Confluence and will be canonical source of truth.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Build data join for CRM/Gainsight, Support tickets, and usage traces, produce candidate features. Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement scorer service in pm-service repo + scoring UI. Phase 3 (3 weeks): Build SLA simulator using BigQuery and the runtime-capacity model; expose read-only UI. Phase 4 (2 weeks): Playbook + approvals + pilot with three strategic accounts. Phase 5: Iteration based on pilot metrics and full rollout.
rollout_plan: Pilot (3 accounts) for 6 weeks -> measure decision latency drop and forecast accuracy -> broaden to top-50 accounts. Communicate via Sales all-hands, update CSM playbook, and schedule training sessions for Solutions Engineers. Lock fast-track rules behind feature flag until post-pilot review.
metrics: Primary: decision latency (hours) for VIP intake, percent of escalations with simulator attached, forecast accuracy for latency delta (MAE ms). Secondary: commitments approved per quarter, SLA regressions attributed to accepted asks, NPS from piloted accounts.

risks:
- Overfitting weights to historical VIPs could bias against emerging accounts.
- Forecast model depends on telemetry retention; if retention window shrinks accuracy will drop.
- Acceptance UI could create expectation of guaranteed delivery; playbook must clarify advisory role and escalation path.
mitigations:
- Regular weight re-calibration cadence (quarterly) and blind holdout tests.
- Require SLO guardrails before any commitment and automatic rollback triggers in release.
- Clear templated language and required stakeholder approvals for any commitment.
